about.size: Up to about 48 in (50 lb) per FWC; Florida state record 45 lb 12 oz
about.diet: Fish and large crustaceans; pinfish, anchovies and shrimp are major prey in one diet study
about.behavior: Ambush predator that faces moving water and waits for prey to be carried down the current. Uses mangrove shorelines, seagrass, beaches, river mouths, docks and other structure. Retreats to deeper channels, backcountry bays and rivers during cold fronts.
about.spawning: April through October in Florida, with peaks around June to September. Spawning aggregations form at inlets, passes, river mouths and nearshore reefs, with eggs released in the late afternoon and early evening on all tides. Atlantic-coast examples named by FWC include Jupiter and Lake Worth inlets.
about.timing_note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs.

reasons.text: This is an inlet. Snook gather in inlets and passes to ambush bait on the tide, and to spawn in summer.
